title: The Lost Courier
tagline: A sealed letter, three strangers and a message that must arrive.
opening: A letter was given to a courier, and the courier never arrived. Somebody, somewhere, is still waiting for it. Let us see who.
ending: The letter reached the hand it was meant for, and the world is a little less lost for it.

postmaster.name: Aldis the Postmaster
lines: No courier has come through in days. I fear the worst.
If you find the letter, do not open it.

courier.name: Wren the Courier
lines: I ran. I am not proud of it, but I ran.
Take the letter. Take it to the one it was meant for.

reader.name: Sage Orrin
lines: Letters from the old road. Rare, these days.
Whoever sent this knew more than they wrote.

steps.tell: The postmaster in {area} is beside himself. Find Aldis, and hear what happened.
says: A courier left here three days ago with a sealed letter, and has not been seen since.
She was last bound for the lands beyond. Find her, if you can, and the letter with her.

steps.tell: Whatever stopped the courier is still out there in {area}. Clear the road before you follow it.
A frightened traveller is hiding in {area}. Find Wren the courier.
says: You came for the letter. Good. I could not carry it another step.
It is for the old sage who keeps the lore. Please, see it into their hands.

steps.tell: The sage the letter is for lives in {area}. Carry the Sealed Letter there and give it over.
says: Ah. So it has come at last. You have done more than you know.
What it says is not for you, but this I will tell you: the roads will be safer for it.

title: The Silent Bell
tagline: A bell that stopped ringing, a keeper with a secret, a trail to follow.
opening: There was a bell in the lands that rang every dusk. It has gone silent, and the silence has begun to spread.
ending: The bell rang again at dusk, and everyone who heard it knew the long silence was over.

ringer.name: Old Maren the Ringer
lines: Forty years I rang that bell. Now there is only quiet.
Find what took the clapper, and bring it home.

smith.name: Dorrin Ashhand
lines: I mend what breaks, but I cannot mend what is missing.
Bring me the clapper and the bell will sing.

steps.tell: The bell-ringer in {area} has a sorrow to tell. Find Old Maren.
says: The bell hangs there still, but its voice is gone. The clapper was taken in the night.
Whoever took it left tracks heading out. Follow them.

steps.tell: The tracks end in {area}. The clapper is hidden somewhere near. Search the land until you have it.
Whatever carried it off has made its den in {area}, and it will not give the clapper up without a fight.
Take the clapper to the smith in {area}. Find Dorrin Ashhand.
says: A fine piece, and nearly whole. Give me a moment at the anvil.
There. Carry it back to the bell, and may it ring true.

steps.tell: The bell hangs where it always did, in {area}. Return the clapper to it, and let it ring.

title: The Wanderer's Debt
tagline: A stranger owes a favour to someone he has never met, and you are the road between.
opening: A wanderer on the road owes a debt he cannot pay. Perhaps you can pay it for him, and learn something on the way.
ending: The debt is paid, the wanderer is free, and two strangers parted as friends.

wanderer.name: Corwin the Wanderer
lines: I owe someone a debt, and I do not even know their face.
They live beyond the next land, so I am told.

creditor.name: Keeper Hale
lines: A debt? I had forgotten it entirely.
Odd, to be repaid by strangers.

steps.tell: A traveller in {area} is looking for help with a debt. Find Corwin.
says: Take these coins, friends. They are what I owe, and a little more.
The one I owe lives some way off. Please, find them. I cannot.

steps.tell: On the road to the creditor, {area} offers what a gift ought to have beside it. Gather it as you pass.
The creditor is in {area}. Find Keeper Hale, and settle the debt.
says: These are the old coins, aren't they? My grandmother's pouch.
Tell Corwin the debt is paid, and something more besides. He is welcome at my fire.
